reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the initial formation of a metastable solid solution with extended solubility via non-equilibrium processing, but provides no data on subsequent thermal aging, precipitation kinetics, or the link between precipitate size/distribution and oxidation/corrosion resistance. The key mechanistic premises about diffusion-controlled transformation and the effect of coarsening on passivation are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Mg-Ti-Zn alloys can be processed into a metastable solid solution via non-equilibrium methods
Thermal exposure causes diffusion-controlled nucleation and growth of intermetallics from this metastable state
Fine, uniform intermetallic precipitates do not deplete the matrix of passivating elements (Mg, Ti, Zn)
A continuous, protective oxide film requires sufficient passivating elements in the matrix
Excessive coarsening of intermetallics depletes passivating elements and disrupts the oxide scale
